artikel.titel: Europe’s Pitch Book: Romania - the gifted one
artikel.text: ROMANIA: Romania belongs in Europe’s Pitch Book as an example of tremendous upside potential. It has the people, energy, technology, land and location. We admit there’s a caveat: Romania needs the confidence and coordination to capitalise on them

artikel.titel: National Bank of Poland to hold rates as inflation pressures remain contained
artikel.text: CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE: The NBP is likely to leave rates at 3.75% on 4 November as underlying inflation pressures remain contained. Attention will focus on the new inflation projection and energy price risks, but we expect rates to stay unchanged through the end of 2026 before 50bp of hikes in 1Q27

artikel.titel: Belgium’s budget crisis is serious, but not hopeless
artikel.text: EUROPE: Belgium's budget talks have hit a wall, but the crisis is not yet at a dead end. A deal on €10 billion in savings remains our base case, though political red lines need to soften. A watered-down compromise would leave debt risks unresolved, while a government collapse could put investor confidence under pressure

artikel.titel: Turkish inflation edges higher as downtrend stalls
artikel.text: CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE: Slightly higher-than-expected October CPI data led to a break in Turkey's inflation downtrend, exposing continued challenges to disinflation efforts

artikel.titel: FX Daily: Democratic sweep can weigh on the dollar
artikel.text: We don’t expect today’s US midterm results to cause structural shifts in FX, but the dollar may face some short-term pressure should the Democrats secure both the House (widely expected) and the Senate (close call). Elsewhere, a dovish hike by the RBA has hit AUD, but we remain optimistic on the outlook for the currency beyond the near term

artikel.titel: The Commodities Feed: False US-Iran hopes or the real deal?
artikel.text: Oil and gas sold off yesterday amid positive signs for US-Iran talks ahead of today’s US midterm elections

artikel.titel: Rates Spark: US midterms and expanding European government bond concerns
artikel.text: Tuesday will be nothing more than the day ahead of a much bigger day – Wednesday, by which time we'll have guidance on the midterm implications, and we'll have the US refunding announcement. In Europe, political jitters in Belgium highlight that France is not the only one struggling to consolidate its finances

artikel.titel: US manufacturing benefiting from a strong economy, tech investment, tariffs and energy security
artikel.text: NORTH AMERICA: The manufacturing sector continues to power ahead, boosted by a strong US economy. Other factors are supportive. There is a clear split in performance between fast-growing tech, pharma and transportation sectors versus more labour-intensive, commoditised sectors. Construction activity suggests interest-rate-sensitive sectors are struggling

artikel.titel: Webinar: ING’s global economic outlook for 2027
artikel.text: EUROPE: Join ING’s economists on 10 November as they share their biggest calls for 2027, plus the risks and surprises that could knock the global economy off course. Sign up here

artikel.titel: Bank of England set for first rate hike as energy shock worsens
artikel.text: EUROPE: We expect a 7-2 vote to hike rates this week and, barring a collapse in energy prices, we think a follow-up move in February is likely too. However, market pricing for the Bank of England still looks extreme
